literal: Not-lying like fame there-is-not; effortlessly all virtue it-will-give.
translation: There is no fame equal to that of never lying; without any effort, it will yield every other virtue.
modern: பொய் சொல்லாமல் இருத்தலைப் போன்ற புகழ் வேறு இல்லை; அது ஒருவருக்கு எந்தவிதமான சோர்வும் முயற்சியும் இல்லாமல் எல்லா அறங்களையும் தரும்.
explanation: The couplet highlights the supreme value of truthfulness by stating that there is no greater glory than maintaining it. The word 'poyyāmai' refers to the practice of never uttering falsehoods. The poet asserts that this single practice is so powerful that it effortlessly ('eyyāmai', meaning without fatigue or struggle) brings about all other virtues ('ellā aṟamum') to a person. Thus, by simply adhering to truth, one naturally attains the fruits of all other righteous deeds without having to strive for them individually.
